meta.study: Guinea DRE study, GEP-OnSSET scenario matrix (Table 1 plus two demand variants)
notes: Hydro mini-grids are only viable within 10 km of a hydro site. This is hard-coded in gep_onsset/onsset.py (max_hydro_dist) and is not a lever.
Mini-hydro sites above 1 MW are excluded upstream: the extraction used a layer filtered at 1 MW or below, so the Hydropower column holds 0 to 1000 kW only. Not a lever.
Grid generation cost levels. 0.1 USD/kWh is the reference and the defaults value; 0.078 the low variant; 0.22 the high variant; 0.047 a legacy level kept for continuity with the earlier runs.
Run order is the batch order. The five demand cases at the reference cost come first, then the three Table 1 cases at the other cost levels in ascending order.
Calibration-stage levers live in the calibration block and cannot be overridden per scenario. One control file has one calibration.
Inputs and outputs under GuineaRuns/ are never committed.

Recorded-only keys. existing_grid_cost_ratio, mv_increase_rate and max_mv_line_dist are written to the Variables file for documentation but never reach the model calls, exactly as in the notebook; prioritization must be 5 because the notebook hard-codes 5 in its model calls.

Supply-side variants (2026-10-25). optgrid removes the 127,000 connections and 90 MW per year caps to 2030 (full grid expansion); optgrid_optmg adds mg_pv_hybrid_cost_factor 0.75 (PV panels of the PV-battery mini-grid 25 percent cheaper, battery and inverter unchanged). Run for the three Table 1 cases at the reference cost.
Key scenarios agreed with the team (2026-10-25): U3R1 (TD_Low_minus), U4R2 (TD_High_minus, urban tier 4, rural tier 2) and BU; they carry the full cost sweep and both supply-side variants.

Grid cost bins (2026-10-25): the bottom-up case is also run at 0.06, 0.12, 0.14, 0.16, 0.18, 0.20 and 0.25 USD/kWh to map how the technology mix moves with the grid generation cost (heat maps in the sensitivity chapter).
